mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months is associated with reduced consumer confidence and corporate earnings pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 6% for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of four consecutive months of INDPRO < -0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL (CPI) and FEDFUNDS above their respective 12-month averages signals an inflationary shock accompanied by a hawkish policy response, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as markets anticipate growth-oriented policy responses.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such dual triggers (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month in the prior two months, combined with a stable unemployment rate, signals robust labor market expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > +1% for 2 consecutive months AND UNRATE stable (change < 0.1pp)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month average, coupled with a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1), signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a slowdown in economic activity and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 5% for three consecutive months signals a recovery in residential construction demand, which boosts materials and homebuilding equities and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of three consecutive months of HOUST > +5% (t-test p > 0.05).
